Cost is 100 SAR per child, paid on the day, and a parent must stay for the whole event. Children need hiking shoes, a hat, a filled water bottle and a nut-free packed lunch, and those without shoes and a hat cannot take part. Register early through the online form, one per child.

All students aged 5 to 11 are invited, Scouts or not, with hands-on radio alphabet, Morse code and two-way radio activities. Families reserve a spot through the online page shared by the school. An online Scout meeting follows on Sat 17 Oct at 11:00 am.

Activities include radio alphabet, Morse code and two-way radios. Families reserve a spot through the online page shared by the school. An online Scout meeting follows on Sat 17 Oct at 11:00 am.

items.body: Final reminder that Scout Pack 257's Jamboree on the Air is at school on Friday 16 Oct 2026, 1:00 to 3:00 pm. A preparation link was shared by the school to help children learn about communication before Friday and Saturday. It is also useful for children who cannot attend.

items.body: A student may show as absent in the Conference section of Edunation even after attending every lesson. That section records attendance through individual student accounts, which are still being set up for Primary students. items.title: Bullying awareness session

items.body: Classroom doors open at 7:40 am and students should be in class by 7:45 am at the latest. Some students keep playing in the playground until 8:00 am and miss Circle Time, which starts at 7:45 am. Families are asked to make sure children enter and join their class on time.
items.title: Morning routine: Circle Time at 7:45 AM

Parents should help children follow teacher instructions promptly.
items.title: Reminder: Online Learning Safety Procedure During Civil Defence Alerts

items.title: Club registration reminder: limited spaces

items.body: The school thanked students, families and staff for their resilience and kindness during the past two weeks of online learning. It wished everyone a restful and happy half-term break. No action is needed from families.

items.title: Personal hygiene awareness

items.title: Saudi National Day celebration, 22 Sep

items.title: Nut-free school policy

items.body: Campuses closed on Ministry guidance. Teachers shared handouts in the morning, official online classes started the next day.
items.title: Online learning arrangements

items.body: Mute microphones when talking to family or when there is background noise. Send questions for the teacher through the Edunation messaging app after the lesson ends. Family members who appear on camera should be dressed appropriately, and students should not eat during lessons, only at break times. Keep Edunation push notifications switched on.
items.title: Online classes: reminders for parents

items.body: Following the latest Ministry of Education directives, online learning continues from Sunday 18 Oct to Thursday 22 Oct 2026. Students stay at home and all lessons are delivered online through Edunation and Zoom. Families should follow the updated online timetable already shared on Edunation.
items.title: Online learning extended, 18 to 22 Oct

items.body: The school shared a parent poster with tips to help children learn well during online classes. It covers getting ready before class, supporting your child during class, healthy routines after class and who to contact for help. Learners are asked to act respectfully, and a teacher may remove a learner who behaves inappropriately. For technical or attendance issues, message the homeroom or relevant teacher on Edunation.
items.title: Guide to online learning for parents

items.body: Families are asked to set up a bright, organised learning space with books and stationery ready before each lesson. Students should keep cameras on throughout lessons unless the teacher says otherwise. Parents should stay quiet and let teachers lead live sessions without interruption, and send any concerns or feedback through Edunation instead. Younger learners may need extra parental support to settle in.
items.title: Guidelines for a positive online learning environment

items.body: Following Ministry of Education directives, the school moved to online learning on Sunday 11 October 2026. Students stay home and do not attend campus. All lessons are delivered remotely through Edunation. Further updates on school operations will be shared as needed.
items.title: Online learning, Sunday 11 Oct

items.body: The school shared its Online Learning Rules and etiquette document with parents. Families are asked to go through it with their child and help them understand the importance of being ready, respectful and responsible during online classes.
items.title: Online class rules and etiquette

items.body: To give students more time away from screens, each online lesson is now 35 minutes, with the usual 10-minute breaks between lessons. Two longer breaks were added: 10:05 to 10:30 and 11:50 to 12:10. The school day stays 8:00 am to 1:30 pm. The new timings are already updated on Edunation.
items.title: Online learning timetable updates for the coming week

items.body: Students should be ready before the first lesson, seated in a quiet place with a charged device and stable internet. Keep the camera on, stay seated and follow the teacher's instructions. The online timetable differs slightly from usual, with a 10-minute break between lessons. A short tutorial video on logging in to Edunation and joining classes was attached.
items.title: Online classes: reminders and tutorial video

items.body: Online learning will continue until further notice, in line with the latest Ministry of Education guidance. The school will share any change to the arrangements with all families promptly through Edunation.
items.title: Online learning continues until further notice

items.body: The class teacher is using a Padlet page to keep students' submitted work in one place during online learning. Last week's spelling test and maths practice are already there under each child's name. Parents are asked to upload this week's spelling test too, even if it was already sent. Feedback and marks stay private on Edunation, and new columns will be added for future work.
items.title: Upload Year 5 online work to the class Padlet

items.body: The school is introducing an Authorised Pick-Up Card for families whose child is regularly collected by a driver, nanny or other authorised person. EduPik through Edunation continues as usual, and a pick-up request must still be created when the child is ready. The card shows the person's photo and details plus the names and classes of the children they may collect. To request one, complete the school's online form with a clear photo, one form per person, and tell the school in advance if the collector changes.
items.title: Authorised Pick-Up Card for drivers and nannies

items.body: The school marks Pink Day today, with children wearing pink to spread kindness and hope. The message is that even the smallest act of kindness can brighten someone's day. No action is needed from families.
items.title: Pink Day today, Thu 22 Oct

items.body: Thursday 22 Oct is the last day of online learning before the term break, and it is Pink Day, so children wear something pink. Families are invited to record a short video of their child in an online lesson and send it to the school front desk. With permission, the school may feature these moments on its official social media.
items.title: Pink Day tomorrow and share a video of online learning

items.body: The school nurse shared a notice after the Ministry of Health reported more respiratory infections this viral season. Families are encouraged to consider the seasonal flu vaccine, teach good hand hygiene and covering coughs, and avoid sharing personal items. Children with flu-like symptoms should stay home until they recover, and families should seek medical advice if symptoms are severe or persistent.
items.title: Health notice: respiratory viruses

items.body: School back on campus 28 Sep. Arrive on time, return textbooks and handouts, buses run as normal, no clubs due to the IB visit.
items.title: Regular on-campus classes resume

Lessons resume once it is confirmed safe, and children should follow teacher instructions promptly.

items.body: The school reassured families that all students are safe, well and fully accounted for. Staff are supervising students, monitoring the situation in real time and in contact with the relevant authorities. Any further updates or instructions will be shared through the Edunation app.

items.body: English: biographies and autobiographies, key features and pair work. Maths: numbers in standard, word and expanded form, plus a Saudi Arabia shape project with number facts. Science: seedlings and how plants begin to grow. Drama: Martin Luther King Jr.'s speech and rights and responsibilities. A new student was named Student of the Week.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 2

items.body:
English, Drama and Unit of Inquiry: monologues and biographies, speaking and performance skills.
Maths: numbers in standard, word and expanded form, counting in powers of 10.
Science: pollination, seedlings and early plant growth.
Highlight: Saudi National Day celebration.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 3

items.body: Wrapping up the Who We Are unit: students studied five activists, presented freeze-frames and are writing and performing monologues. Maths: comparing numbers up to one million, negative numbers and a mental-arithmetic test. Science: seeds were planted and will be observed over the coming week. Highlight: the IB observation lesson went very well.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 4

items.body: Maths: Roman numerals and rounding numbers up to one million. Science: classroom plant observations finished and the plants went home to keep growing. The first Unit of Inquiry, Who We Are, closed with an assembly where students shared projects, freeze-frames and monologues. Photos and short videos of the assembly were attached to the email.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 5

items.body: English: the class began reading The Boy at the Back of the Class, linked to the new Unit of Inquiry, Where We Are in Place and Time (migration, belonging, friendship). Families are encouraged to get their child their own copy if possible. Science: the Earth's orbit and seasons. Maths: column addition, with column subtraction next week. Also covered: global trade in Global Citizenship, Britain's past and present in History, and friendship and inclusion in PSHE.
